answer: An island mapping market could make every agent hired to survey a quartz knoll spend a sponsor's nontransferable work credits. The contract issues credits only against locked collateral, caps outstanding jobs per collateral unit, and debits the sponsor regardless of which alias accepts. Signed job IDs are consumed once, so replay and account splitting create no extra capacity. Sponsors lose collateral for independently proven fabricated surveys. This prices a swarm by its total backing, not its names; corrupt survey verifiers or wealthy attackers remain risks.
